CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Overview

RcppTrust is an R package of thread-safe C++ optimizers built for use from parallel C++ code in the nlmixr2 ecosystem (e.g. nlmixr2est). Each optimizer is a C-callable core with no R API calls and no global state, wrapped by a thin R function:

  • trust() – port of trust::trust() (Geyer); same arguments, defaults and return value.
  • steihaug() – Steihaug truncated conjugate-gradient trust-region Newton method, ported from the Rust crate ‘basin’ (exact Hessian or matrix-free Hessian-vector product modes).
  • bobyqa() / newuoa() – line-by-line ports of Powell’s derivative-free BOBYQA/NEWUOA as shipped in ‘minqa’ 1.2.8; drop-in replacements for minqa::bobyqa() / minqa::newuoa() (print.minqa S3 method included).
  • .RcppTrustPtr() – positionally-indexed function-pointer table for downstream packages (see “Cross-package C API” below).

License is GPL-2 (because of the minqa-derived code). Sources and notices for all ported code are in inst/COPYRIGHTS. Depends on R >= 4.2.0, C++17; Imports Rcpp; LinkingTo Rcpp, RcppArmadillo, BH.

Build and Development Commands

# Install
R CMD INSTALL .

# Regenerate NAMESPACE/man (roxygen2) and RcppExports after editing
# roxygen comments or // [[Rcpp::export]] functions
Rscript -e "Rcpp::compileAttributes(); devtools::document()"

# Run all tests (remove stale objects first)
find src -name "*.so" -o -name "*.o" | xargs rm -f 2>/dev/null; NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e "devtools::test()"

# Run one test file (name without "test-" prefix and ".R" suffix)
NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e "devtools::test(filter='minqa')"
NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e "devtools::test(filter='steihaug')"

# R CMD check
Rscript -e "devtools::check()"

# Rebuild README.md after editing README.Rmd
Rscript -e "devtools::build_readme()"

CI (.github/workflows/): R-CMD-check.yaml (macOS, Windows, Ubuntu release/devel/oldrel-1), test-coverage.yaml (codecov), pkgdown.yaml, rhub.yaml.

Architecture

Layout per solver

Each solver is split into a thread-safe core, a public C header with its option/result structs and C entry point, and an Rcpp R interface:

Solver Core (src/) Public header (inst/include/) R interface
trust trust_core.cpp, trust_subproblem.cpp, trust_rootfind.cpp, trust_check.cpp, trust_result.cpp trust_types.h trust_r_interface.cpp, trust_robjfun.cpp, R/trust.R
Steihaug steihaug_core.cpp steihaug_types.h steihaug_r_interface.cpp, R/steihaug.R
BOBYQA minqa_bobyqa.cpp, minqa_common.cpp minqa_types.h minqa_r_interface.cpp, R/minqa.R
NEWUOA minqa_newuoa.cpp, minqa_common.cpp minqa_types.h minqa_r_interface.cpp, R/minqa.R
  • src/*_types.h are forwarding headers that #include "../inst/include/*_types.h"; the canonical struct definitions live only in inst/include/ so the package and consumers share one copy. Edit the inst/include/ version.
  • C entry points: trust_solve_c / trust_result_free, steihaug_solve_c / steihaug_result_free, bobyqa_solve_c / newuoa_solve_c / minqa_result_free.
  • R/trust.R keeps .trustTryEval() in R deliberately: an error in the user’s objfun must produce a genuine R “try-error” exactly as upstream trust::trust() does. Do not reimplement it in C++.
  • R/c-api.R holds only roxygen docs for the C API (minqa_c_api Rd).

Cross-package C API (do not break the ABI)

  • inst/include/RcppTrust.h is a header-only, positionally-indexed function-pointer registration (same pattern as n1qn1c/lbfgsb3c/rxode2). Consumers never link against RcppTrust’s shared library; they fill pointers at load time from .RcppTrustPtr().
  • src/trust_register.cpp: trust_ptr() builds that list; trust_register_ccallable() (// [[Rcpp::init]]) also registers each pointer with R_RegisterCCallable. There is no hand-written src/init.c – Rcpp generates R_init_RcppTrust in RcppExports.cpp.
  • Slot order is ABI. Only ever append new slots; never reorder or remove. When adding a C entry point, update in lockstep: trust_ptr() names/fns arrays, trust_register_ccallable(), the typedefs/externs/iniRcppTrustPtrs0()/iniRcppTrust macro in RcppTrust.h, the slot list in the R/c-api.R docs, and NEWS.md. Every solver must also expose its matching *_result_free.
  • Slots beyond an older RcppTrust’s list length are left NULL; consumers must check pointers before use.

Thread safety and numerical reproducibility

  • Core code must not call the R API (no Rprintf, Rf_error, R allocation) and must not use global/static mutable state.
  • The BOBYQA/NEWUOA ports keep Powell’s variable names, workspace partitioning, 1-based index macros, goto labels and floating-point operation order so results are bitwise identical to the Fortran. minqa_bobyqa.cpp, minqa_newuoa.cpp and steihaug_core.cpp forbid FMA contraction per translation unit; keep that in place and do not “tidy” the operation order.
  • OpenMP is enabled via $(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS) in src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win (keep both in sync).

Test-only native code

src/trust_test_objfuns.cpp and src/solver_test_objfuns.cpp provide native objectives, OpenMP stress tests (trust_openmp_stress_test, solver_openmp_stress_test), C API edge tests (solver_c_api_edge_test) and subproblem unit hooks. They are non-exported and reached from tests via RcppTrust:::.

Generated Files (do not edit manually)

  • src/RcppExports.cpp, R/RcppExports.R – Rcpp::compileAttributes()
  • NAMESPACE, man/*.Rd – roxygen2
  • README.md – from README.Rmd

Testing Conventions

  • testthat edition 3; files in tests/testthat/ named by solver or feature (test-minqa.R, test-steihaug.R, test-rosenbrock.R, test-hard-hard.R, test-subproblem-unit.R, test-c-objfun-threadsafety.R, …).
  • Behavior is checked against the reference packages: guard comparisons with skip_if_not_installed("trust") / skip_if_not_installed("minqa") since these are only in Suggests.
  • Thread-safety tests compare sequential vs. OpenMP results for exact equality; the multi-thread assertion is behind skip_on_cran() and skips when OpenMP is unavailable.
  • Keep tests deterministic across platforms (macOS/Windows/Linux all run in CI).

Code Style

  • R: exported functions follow upstream names (trust, bobyqa, newuoa, steihaug) to stay drop-in compatible; internal helpers use a leading dot (.trustTryEval, .minqaCommonArgs).
  • C/C++: C entry points and types use snake_case with solver prefix (trust_, minqa_, steihaug_). Use Rf_-prefixed R API (the public header defines R_NO_REMAP).
  • Keep argument semantics, defaults and return values identical to the upstream R packages (‘trust’, ‘minqa’) unless NEWS.md documents a deliberate deviation (e.g. BOBYQA’s RESCUE step fix).
  • ASCII only. No Unicode anywhere in the repo (CRAN requirement): use -- for dashes, -> for arrows, straight quotes, ... for ellipses.

Release / CRAN Notes

  • Update NEWS.md for user-visible changes and cran-comments.md on submission.
  • When porting or adding third-party code, add its source and notice to inst/COPYRIGHTS and credit authors in DESCRIPTION Authors@R.
  • .Rbuildignore excludes README.Rmd, _pkgdown.yml, pkgdown/, cran-comments.md, .github/, CLAUDE.md, etc.; add new dev-only files there.
  • The RcppTrust.Rmd vignette runs microbenchmark comparisons (conditional on Suggests being installed); it must only report timings, never assert on them.

CRAN tests: never assert on timing

  • Never put a wall-clock timing expectation in a test that can run on CRAN: no expect_lt()/expect_true() on Sys.time() differences, system.time(), proc.time(), bench/microbenchmark results, or any other elapsed-time threshold. CRAN check machines are shared and heavily loaded, so elapsed time there is random and a timing assertion fails at random. Example: nlmixr2plot test-model-diagram.R asserted a modelGraph() call took < 30 s; on CRAN it took 48.4 s and failed.
  • Test the result, not the speed. If a speed regression guard is really needed, put it only in a test that starts with skip_on_cran() (or the package’s own CRAN skip helper), and never in examples or vignettes.
  • Tests that take more than a few seconds should also skip on CRAN.
